citation: "Early Chicago Voter Lists" — the poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago (10 August 1833), the tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833, the election returns and poll list of 1834 filed 11 August 1834, and the 1835 poll list. Transcribed from the Illinois Regional Archives Depository originals by Ingrid Latimer Schulz, published in Chicago Genealogist XXV/4 (Summer 1993), and republished by the Genealogy Trails Transcription Team.
author: Ingrid Latimer Schulz (transcriber); Genealogy Trails Transcription Team
repository: Illinois Regional Archives Depository (IRAD) holds the originals; this project has seen only the republication and the deposit copy
locator: chicago/reference/voter-roll/ — the transcription (.txt and .docx) and the supplied PDF; the same text is committed byte-identical at chicago/4d/data/research/civic/text/voter_lists_1833_1835.txt, and every record's locator names its line there

transcribes.work: Poll list for the first election of Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago (10 August 1833)
transcribes.note: 30 entries. Andreas says twenty-eight men voted at this election; the list prints thirty names, and the discrepancy is recorded rather than repaired (claims/town_findings_andreas_v1.json c002).

transcribes.work: Tax List of the Town of Chicago - 1833
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Names only — as published it carries no valuation, no lot and no figure, so it is not a ranked property roll (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v001).

transcribes.work: Election Returns - Poll List of 1834, filed 11 August 1834
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Andreas independently dates the second town election to 11 August 1834, which corroborates the list's own heading.

85 entries. THE LIST PRINTS NO DATE. Andreas contradicts himself on which election it was: 'The third election was held in July, 1835' in the town chapter, and 'the third election of town oHicers, which occurred August 5, 1835' in the police chapter. The scene date is 1835-07-01, so the poll falls either within days of it or 35 days after; nothing seen decides which, and T-0513 inherits the question.

access_notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-03 by fetching the live Genealogy Trails page and comparing it with the deposit entry for entry: all 345 entries appear on the page, in the same order, with the same spelling, and the page carries no entry the deposit lacks. That verifies the DEPOSIT against the publication. It does NOT verify the publication against the IRAD originals, which remain unseen — the reading is mediated twice, by Schulz and then by the Genealogy Trails team, and every record citing this source is graded `transcription_mediated`. The page answers a browser user-agent; a default one is refused with HTTP 406.
what_it_supplies: 345 names of men who voted at, or were taxed by, the Town of Chicago in 1833, 1834 and 1835, as printed
which of the four lists each name stands on, and its position in that list
the courtesy and rank titles the lists print in front of a name (Col., Lt., Major, Dr.)
for the 1835 poll list: presence in Chicago during 1835, which is the strongest residence evidence this project holds short of a newspaper naming the man
what_it_does_not_supply: any address, street, lot or dwelling
any age, trade, household or family member
any date more precise than a list's own heading — and the 1835 list has no heading date at all
any woman, and any man who neither voted nor was taxed
note: A poll list records who VOTED, not who lived in the town: absence from it is not absence from Chicago. Spellings are the transcription's and are preserved exactly, including the ambiguous 'S---?, Albert' in the 1834 list and the apparent misprints 'Smow, George W.' (1833) and 'Shatttuck, Walter' (1835) — repairing them is a reading and belongs to the identity layer, not to the record. The tier carried here is the rung the DOCUMENTS sit on; the reading of them is twice mediated and is graded on every record that cites it.
